questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “SSR Performance”?
options: SSR Performance helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
SSR Performance means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
SSR Performance removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
SSR Performance should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: SSR Performance helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: SSR Performance is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Server rendering latency” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Server rendering latency” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Server rendering latency” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Server rendering latency” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Server rendering latency” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Server rendering latency” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Server rendering latency” under SSR Performance. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “SSR Performance”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
